data.long_meaning: Bhagtej is a Sanskrit name derived from the word Bhagati, which means 'devotee' or 'worshiper'. The name Bhagtej is used to signify the one who is the lord of wealth and prosperity. In Hindu mythology, Bhagtej is an epithet of Lord Vishnu, who is considered the preserver of the universe and the giver of all wealth and blessings. The name is also considered auspicious and is bestowed upon children to bring them prosperity and good fortune.

historical_references.reference: Bhagtej was a legendary king of the Trigarta kingdom in northern India, mentioned in the Mahabharata epic. He was the father of three powerful brothers: Bhishma, Dhritarashtra, and Vidura. Bhagtej is also known as Shantanu.

Bhagtej was a major god in the Hindu pantheon, identified with the Vedic god Dyaus Pita or the god of the sky. He is often depicted riding a chariot pulled by white horses and holding a bow. Bhagtej is believed to have granted the Devi Durga her weapon, the 'Trishula' or trident.
